name: Hashing
summary: Turn a 'have I seen this before?' question into an average O(1) lookup. Scan the input once, remember what is already known, and answer each element with a lookup instead of a search. The same idea covers prefix sums: remember prefix totals so any range becomes one subtraction.
signal: counts, complements, fast lookup, 'have I seen this value before?'
mentalModel: I need fast lookup. What have I already seen?
recognitionRules: The question can be rewritten as 'have I seen this value before?'
A brute force solution needs a nested scan (O(n^2)) only to search for a value.
You can compute the value you need from the current element (target - current, prefix sum, frequency).
The answer only needs a count or an index, not a sorted order.
Duplicates matter and you need to count, group, or deduplicate them.
The question asks for a sum, count or average over a contiguous range (prefix sums).
invariant: The data structure represents exactly the information seen so far, and nothing else.
